STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r1.speaker: Most scholars
STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r1.claim: Most scholars consider the whole sūrah Makkan.
STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r1.anchor: all of al-Raḥmān to be a Makkan sūrah,

STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r3.speaker: A minority
STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r3.claim: A minority considers the entire sūrah Madinan.
STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r3.anchor: A minority maintain that the entire sūrah is Madinan

STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r12.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r12.claim: Verse 27 is echoed by verse 78, showing that God transcends both earthly and heavenly blessings.
STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r12.anchor: V. 27 is then echoed in the last verse (v. 78)

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p105/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p105/r1.speaker: Some people
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p105/r1.claim: Some classify Sūrah al-Raḥmān as Madinan.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p105/r1.anchor: Some people have regarded this sūrah to be Madīnan

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p105/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p105/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p105/r2.claim: The author rejects a Madinan classification, arguing that no verse appears to be Madinan and the whole sūrah shares one tone and rhythm.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p105/r2.anchor: a single verse of it appears to be Mad īnan much less the whole sūrah

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p105/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p105/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p105/r3.claim: The sūrah’s Makkan opponents demand a punishment sign before accepting that rejection brings punishment and everlasting humiliation in the Hereafter.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p105/r3.anchor: his opponents, in their fury to refute him, had become adamant on a demand: unless a sign of punishment was shown to them

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p105/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p105/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p105/r5.claim: The preceding Sūrah al-Qamar taught Quraysh to learn from messengers and their history rather than insist on seeing punishment; revelation itself is a favor for education and remembrance.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p105/r5.anchor: In Sūrah al-Qamar, the obdurate people of the Quraysh were told to learn a lesson from messengers and the history of their people

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p110/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p110/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p110/r5.claim: The sūrah distinguishes the characteristics of Paradise for the muqarrabīn from those for the asḥāb al-yamīn.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p110/r5.anchor: the muqarrabīn shall receive are delineated, followed by the features and characteristics of the Paradise which the asḥāb al-yamīn will be blessed with

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p120/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p120/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p120/r5.claim: The repeated phrase ‘Lord of majesty and bounty’ at the end of the sūrah indicates that only God is exalted, revered, and without a partner in these attributes.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p120/r5.anchor: The purpose of mentioning both these words is that only He is exalted in His being and thus only He is worthy of being respected and revered by all.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p132/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p132/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p132/r3.claim: The closing blessing repeats after the reward passage because the Lord's majesty guarantees these favours; God's name signifies His being, as face did earlier.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p132/r3.anchor: The name signifies the entity it stands for.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p53/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p53/r1.speaker: الخليل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p53/r1.claim: He defines العبقري as anything noble and precious among people or other things; الجلال means greatness, illustrated by an anonymous poem.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p53/r1.anchor: وقال الخليل: العبقري: كل جليل نفيس من الرجال والنساء وغيرهم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p72/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p72/r2.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p72/r2.claim: Most readers make dhu al-jalāl an adjective for rabb; Ibn ʿĀmir and the Syrians make dhaw an adjective for the name, with further variant forms transmitted.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p72/r2.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: ذي الجلال: صفة لربك وابن عامر وأهل الشام: ذو صفة للاسم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p72/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p72/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p72/r3.claim: Here al-ism means the named entity; another view treats the word name as redundant, as face may be in the verse about the Lord's face.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p72/r3.anchor: والمراد هنا بالاسم المسمى. وقيل: اسم مقحم، كالوجه في ويبقى وجه ربك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p72/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p72/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p72/r4.claim: Blessing can be predicated of the name as elevation; if the name is elevated, the named Lord is all the more worthy of elevation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p72/r4.anchor: وقد صح الإسناد إلى الاسم لأنه بمعنى العلو، فإذا علا الاسم، فما ظنك بالمسمى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p72/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p72/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p72/r5.claim: The ending of worldly blessings with the enduring face matches the end of afterlife blessings with the blessed name: permanence suits the world's passing, while growth suits the increase and duration of Paradise's gifts.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p72/r5.anchor: ختم تعالى نعم الدنيا بقوله: ويبقى وجه ربك ذو الجلال والإكرام، ختم نعم الآخرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p72/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p72/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p72/r6.claim: The Prophet taught people to invoke God by the name dhu al-jalāl wa-l-ikrām.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p72/r6.anchor: قال صلى الله عليه وسلم: «ألظوا بيا ذا الجلال والإكرام»

ELMALILI:55:76-78#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:76-78#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:55:76-78#2/r10.claim: For the close paired with “Owner of majesty and generosity,” tabaraka most fittingly means exaltation and loftiness; an alternative takes it to mean abundant goodness and blessing.
ELMALILI:55:76-78#2/r10.anchor: Burada {ذِى ٱلْجَلَٰلِ وَٱلْإِكْرَامِ} vasfına enseb olan “tebâreke”, te‘âlî ve yücelik mânasına olmaktır.

ELMALILI:55:76-78#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:76-78#2/r11.speaker: Âlûsî
ELMALILI:55:76-78#2/r11.claim: Alusi says the sense of abundant blessing is also plausible because God's name is invoked when people seek mercy, rescue, victory, and help.
ELMALILI:55:76-78#2/r11.anchor: Âlûsî der ki: “‘Tebareke’ fiilinin bu mânaca ism-i ilâhîye isnâdı da ba‘îd değildir. Çünkü O’nun hürmetine rahmet istenir iğāse olunur

ELMALILI:55:76-78#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:76-78#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:55:76-78#2/r12.claim: Ism can mean any of God's beautiful names, with al-Rahman especially in view because it opened the surah; the name's elevation points first to the exaltation of God's essence, to which the following attribute applies.
ELMALILI:55:76-78#2/r12.anchor: “İsm”i, esmâ-i hüsnâsından her birine sâdıktır. Bununla beraber bilhassa sûrenin başında geçen “er- Rahmân” ism-i şerîfi ilk evvel mülâhaza edilmek lâzım gelir.

ELMALILI:55:76-78#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:76-78#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:55:76-78#2/r13.claim: Ibn Amir's qira'a reads zū as an adjective; this leads some to take ism as inserted and others to understand it as the named essence.
ELMALILI:55:76-78#2/r13.anchor: İbn Âmir kıraatinde ism-i sıfat olarak “Zû” okunur. Bunun için bazıları ismin ثُ َّم اِسْمُ ال َّسَلاَمِ عَلَيْكُمَا gibi mukham olduğuna, bazıları da müsemmâ mânasına olduğuna zâhib olmuşlardır.

ELMALILI:55:76-78#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:76-78#2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:55:76-78#2/r14.claim: The surah that opened with al-Rahman closes with majesty and generosity, and this manifestation is followed by the opening of al-Waqiʿa.
ELMALILI:55:76-78#2/r14.anchor: İşte “er-Rahmân” ismiyle başlayan bu Arûs-ı Kur’an böyle celâl ü ikram ile itmam edilmiş bulunuyor ki, bu celâl ve ikrâmın tecelliyâtından biri olmak üzere Sûre-i Vâkı‘a başlayacaktır.

ASAD-NOTES:55:78/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:55:78/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:55:78/r1.claim: Asad rejects the weak, arbitrary view that two further gardens are for believers of lesser merit; their juxtaposition with the earlier pair instead suggests endless gardens, varied symbols of supreme bliss.
ASAD-NOTES:55:78/r1.anchor: As against this weak and somewhat arbitrary interpretation, it seems to me that the juxtaposition of "two other gardens" with. the "two" previously mentioned is meant to convey the idea of infinity

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:46/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:46/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:46/r3.claim: After examples of afterlife blessings, the closing reminder says attaining God's pleasure is more valuable than all those blessings.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:46/r3.anchor: bütün bu nimetlerden çok daha değerli olan şeyin Allah Teâlâ’nın hoşnutluğuna erme mutluluğu olacağı hatırlatılmış olmaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:46/r19.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:46/r19.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:46/r19.claim: The surah begins with the name al-Rahman and ends by exalting the name of the Lord of majesty and generosity.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:46/r19.anchor: Allah Teâlâ’nın Rahmân ismiyle başlayan sûre, azamet ve kerem sahibi rabbimizin adının ne kadar yüce olduğuna yapılan vurgulu bir ifadeyle sona ermektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:46/r20.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:46/r20.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:46/r20.claim: Inspired by a report from the Messenger, scholars recommend invoking God in prayer by the epithet Dhu al-Jalal wa-l-Ikram, hoping it will help prayers be accepted.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:46/r20.anchor: Âlimler Resûlullah’tan yapılan bir rivayetten esinlenerek, dualarda, Allah’ı burada geçen “zü’l-celâli ve’l-ikrâm” sıfatıyla nitelemeyi tavsiye etmişler

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p253/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p253/r1.speaker: ابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p253/r1.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir alone reads dhū al-jalāli with nominative wāw.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p253/r1.anchor: قال: قرأ ابن عامر وحده: تبارك اسم ربك ذو الجلال [الرحمن/ 78] بالواو

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p253/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p253/r2.speaker: الجميع
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p253/r2.claim: All readers also have the genitive dhī al-jalāli; codices are reported with variant spellings in the regions named.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p253/r2.anchor: وكلهم قرأ: ذي الجلال والإكرام بالياء، وكذلك في مصاحف أهل الحجاز والعراق .

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p253/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p253/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p253/r3.claim: The genitive makes dhī an adjective of rabbika, supported by Ibn Masʿūd’s codex, which has the genitive in both clauses.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p253/r3.anchor: من قال: ذي فجر جعله صفة لربك، وزعموا أن في حرف ابن مسعود: ويبقى وجه ربك ذي الجلال بالياء في كلتيهما.

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p253/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p253/r4.speaker: الأصمعي
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p253/r4.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī says jalāl is used only of God, supporting the genitive; the author counters with a poem applying jalāl to someone else.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p253/r4.anchor: وقال الأصمعي: لا يقال الجلال إلا في الله عز وجل، فهذا يقوي الجر، إلا أن الجلال قد جاء في غير الله

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p253/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p253/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p253/r5.claim: The nominative can be parsed by treating the word as a new nominal subject.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p253/r5.anchor: فالجر الوجه في ذي، ومن رفع أجراه على الاسم

QIRAAT-ER:55:78:4#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:55:78:4#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:55:78:4#1/r1.claim: The nominative dhū makes it an adjective of ism rather than rabb, construing the name itself as possessing majesty and honor instead of describing the Lord.
QIRAAT-ER:55:78:4#1/r1.anchor: Nominative reading (dhū instead of genitive dhī) — makes dhū an adjective of ism

QASHANI:55:76-78/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:55:76-78/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:55:76-78/r3.claim: The blessed name of the Lord is the Supreme Name by which seekers rise from beginning to end until they attain it.
QASHANI:55:76-78/r3.anchor: الاسم الأعظم الذي به تزيد وترتقي مرتبة السالكين من البداية إلى النهاية حتى الوصول إليه والفوز به

QASHANI:55:76-78/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:55:76-78/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:55:76-78/r4.claim: For lovers who subsist after annihilation, majesty appears as beauty and beauty as majesty without either veiling the other; earlier, they veiled each other before realized divine existence and return to the attributes.
QASHANI:55:76-78/r4.anchor: الجلال في صورة الجمال والجمال في صورة الجلال اللذان لا يحجب أحدهما عن الآخر عند البقاء بعد الفناء

ALUSI-FULL:v27p127/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p127/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p127/r1.claim: ‘Tabāraka the name of your Lord’ sanctifies God and confirms the favors enumerated throughout the surah.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p127/r1.anchor: ( وقوله عز وجل : ( تبارك اسم ربك ( تنزيه وتقديس له تعالى فيه تقرير لما ذكر في هذه السورة الكريمة من آلائه

ALUSI-FULL:v27p127/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p127/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p127/r2.claim: Al-Alusi reads tabāraka as ‘exalted’; the name includes al-Raḥmān at the surah’s opening and is far above denial of God’s favors.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p127/r2.anchor: وقدورد في الأحاديث تعالى اسمه أي تعالى اسمه الجليل الذي من جملته ما صدرتبهالسورة من اسم ( الرحمن ) المنبيء عن إفاضة الآلاء المفصلة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p127/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p127/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v27p127/r3.claim: One view takes ‘name’ to mean attribute, since an attribute marks its bearer.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p127/r3.anchor: وقيل : الأسم بمعنى الصفة لأنها علامة على موصوفها

ALUSI-FULL:v27p127/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p127/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v27p127/r4.claim: One view treats ‘name’ as an inserted word, as in the cited formula ‘then the name of peace be upon you both.’
ALUSI-FULL:v27p127/r4.anchor: وقيل : هو مقحم كما في قول من قال : ثم اسم السلام عليكما

ALUSI-FULL:v27p127/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p127/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v27p127/r5.claim: One view takes ‘name’ to mean the named referent.

ALUSI-FULL:v27p127/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p127/r6.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v27p127/r6.claim: Some say the surah’s theme of abundant favors makes ‘tabāraka’ best understood as abundant blessings.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p127/r6.anchor: وزعم بعضهم إن الأنسب بما قصد من هذه السورة الكريمة وهو تعدد الآلاء والنعم تفسير ( تبارك ) بكثرت خيراته

ALUSI-FULL:v27p127/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p127/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p127/r7.claim: Attributing abundant blessings to God’s name is fitting because people invoke it for rain and seek aid through it.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p127/r7.anchor: ثم إنهلا بعدفي إسناده بهذا المعنى لاسمهتعالآ إذا به يستمطر فيغاث ويستنصر فيعان

ALUSI-FULL:v27p127/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p127/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p127/r8.claim: ‘Possessor of majesty and generosity’ describes the Lord and completes the preceding purification and affirmation.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p127/r8.anchor: صفة للرب ووصف جل وعلا بذلك تكميلالما ذكر من التنزيه والتقرير

ALUSI-FULL:v27p127/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p127/r9.speaker: ابن عامر وأهل الشام
ALUSI-FULL:v27p127/r9.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir and Syrian readers recite dhū in the nominative, making it an adjective of ‘name’; majesty and generosity aptly describe it.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p127/r9.anchor: وقرأابن عامر وأهل الشام ذو ج بالرفع على أنه وصف للأسم ووصفه بالجلال والإكرام بمعنى التكريم واضح

ALUSI-FULL:v27p127#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p127#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p127#2/r13.claim: Esoterically, majesty is complete independence from manifestations, while generosity is the universal effusion received according to each receptacle’s capacity.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p127#2/r13.anchor: ذو الجلال ) أي الأستغناء التام عن جميع المظاهر ( والإكرام ) الفيض العام يفيض على القوابل حسبمااستعدت له

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p459#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p459#2/r1.speaker: أهل الشام
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p459#2/r1.claim: The Syrian readers recite dhū al-jalāl with nominative wāw, as in their codices, agreeing it with the divine name.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p459#2/r1.anchor: قرأ أهل الشام "ذو الجلال" بالواو وكذلك هو في مصاحفهم إجراء على الاسم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p459#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p459#2/r2.speaker: عائشة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p459#2/r2.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports that after prayer the Prophet would sit only long enough to say that God is Peace, from Him comes peace, and He is blessed, Possessor of Majesty and Honor.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p459#2/r2.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا سلم من الصلاة لم يقعد إلا مقدار ما يقول

BAYDAWI-FULL:55:71-78/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:71-78/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:71-78/r5.claim: God’s name is exalted because it applies to His essence; if the name is exalted, the essence is all the more so.
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:71-78/r5.anchor: تبرك اسم ربك } تعالى اسمه من حيث إنه مطلق على ذاته فما ظنك لذاته

BAYDAWI-FULL:55:71-78/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:71-78/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:71-78/r6.claim: Alternatively, ism means attribute, or it is an extra word, as in the cited line about the greeting of peace after a year.
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:71-78/r6.anchor: وقيل الاسم بمعنى الصفة أو مقحم كما في قوله:

BAYDAWI-FULL:55:78/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:78/r1.speaker: ابن عامر
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:78/r1.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads dhū in the nominative as an adjective of the word ism.
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:78/r1.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر بالرفع صفة للاسم

BAYDAWI-FULL:55:78/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:78/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:78/r2.claim: A prophetic report says that whoever recites Sūrat al-Raḥmān has fulfilled gratitude for God’s blessings.
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:78/r2.anchor:
عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
" من قرأ سورة الرحمن

SULAMI:v2p298/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p298/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p298/r1.claim: They gloss God's blessedness as exaltation and transcendence above the false claims of unbelievers; every creature's praise is limited by its own capacity and understanding.
SULAMI:v2p298/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : تبارك ربك أي جل ربك وتنزه وعظم قدره عما يقول الملحدون المبطلون جميعا لأن كل مثن يثنى عليه بقدره

SULAMI:v2p298/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p298/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p298/r2.claim: Human praise and knowledge cannot reach God, who exceeds human imagination; even the Prophet says no one can enumerate His praise, and He alone praises Himself fully.
SULAMI:v2p298/r2.anchor: لأن الثناء والمعارف دون الغايات فسبحانه وتعالى عما أثنى عليه غيره ولا وصفه بما يليق به سواه عجزا إلا الأنبياء جميعهم

SULAMI:v2p298/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p298/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
SULAMI:v2p298/r3.claim: The Prophet's supplication says he cannot enumerate God's praise, for God is as He has praised Himself.
SULAMI:v2p298/r3.anchor: حتى قال اجلهم قدرا واعلاهم ذكرا وارفعهم محلا صلى الله عليه وسلم : ' سبحانك لا احصى ثناء عليك أنت كما اثنيت على نفسك '

BIQAI-FULL:v7p399/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p399/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p399/r14.claim: The close of the passage completes eight blessings reserved for the right-hand garden, alluding to its eight gates.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p399/r14.anchor: تمت النعم الثمان المختصة بجنة أصحاب اليمين إشارة إلى العمل لأبوابها الثمانية

BIQAI-FULL:v7p399/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p399/r15.speaker: ابن برجان
BIQAI-FULL:v7p399/r15.claim: Ibn Barjān derives tabāraka from baraka and says God is rarely described with it except in connection with something wondrous.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p399/r15.anchor: قال ابن برجان : تفاعل من البركة , ولا يكاد يذكره جل ذكره إلا عند أمر معجب

BIQAI-FULL:v7p399/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p399/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p399/r16.claim: Tabāraka means enduring in a way no mind can encompass, with blessing and beneficence beyond measure.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p399/r16.anchor: ومعناه ثبت ثباتا لا يسع العقول جمع وصفه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p399/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p399/r17.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p399/r17.claim: Honoring God's name is more emphatic than honoring the named; the Lord is the benefactor who sent the Qur'an and formed the Prophet to follow it.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p399/r17.anchor: ولما كان تعظيم الاسم أقعد وأبلغ في تعظيم المسمى قال : { اسم ربك }

BIQAI-FULL:v7p399/r18.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p399/r18.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p399/r18.claim: Al-jalāl denotes overwhelming majesty and vengeance on enemies, while al-ikrām denotes beneficence and mercy for allies; the paired wording uses reciprocal ellipsis.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p399/r18.anchor: الوصفان الأخيران من شبه الاحتباك حذف من الأول متعلق الصفة وهو النقمة للأعداء

BIQAI-FULL:v7p399/r19.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p399/r19.speaker: ابن عامر
BIQAI-FULL:v7p399/r19.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads dhū rather than the majority's dhī, making it an adjective of the Name; Syrian codices also support this form.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p399/r19.anchor: وقراءة ابن عامر { ذو } صفة للاسم , وكذا هو في مصاحف أهل الشام

BIQAI-FULL:v7p399/r20.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p399/r20.speaker: الرازي
BIQAI-FULL:v7p399/r20.claim: Al-Rāzī says the closing Name refers back to the opening Name of the sūrah, encompassing both Qur'anic teaching and divine punishment.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p399/r20.anchor: وقال الرازي في اللوامع : كأنه يريد بالاسم الذي افتتح به السورة وقد انعطف آخر السورة على أولها

BIQAI-FULL:v7p402/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402/r1.claim: Sūrat al-Wāqiʿa explains the conditions of the three groups mentioned in al-Raḥmān: foremost and later allies, and openly or secretly hostile opponents among humans and jinn.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402/r1.anchor: مقصودها شرح أحوال الأقسام الثلاثة المذكورة في الرحمن للأولياء من السابقين واللاحقين والأعداء المشاققين من المصارحين والمنافقين من الثقلين

BIQAI-FULL:v7p402/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402/r2.claim: The sequence displays complete divine power through freely chosen action: al-Raḥmān ends by affirming perfection, while al-Wāqiʿa ends by denying defect and affirming majesty.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402/r2.anchor: دل عليه آخر الرحمن بإثبات الكمال ودل عليه آخر هذه بالتنزيه بالنفي لكل شيء به نقص

BIQAI-FULL:v7p402/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402/r3.claim: Equal outcomes for all people would undermine eloquent wisdom and give naturalists a pretext for doubt.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402/r3.anchor: ولو استوى الناس لم يكن ذلك من بليغ الحكمة ، فإن استواءهم يكون شبهة لأهل الطبيعة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p402/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402/r4.claim: The name al-Wāqiʿa itself points to the sūrah's purpose when its verses and grammatical attachment are considered.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402/r4.anchor: واسمها الواقعة دال على ذلك بتأمل آياته وما يتعلق الظرف به

BIQAI-FULL:v7p402/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402/r5.claim: The basmala invokes God as the one who assigns people differing conditions.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402/r5.anchor: { بسم الله } الذي له الكمال كله ففاوت بين الناس في الأحوال

BIQAI-FULL:v7p402/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402/r6.claim: Al-Raḥmān gave the gift of expression broadly, while people's reception differs between turning away and accepting.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402/r6.anchor: { الرحمن } الذي عم بنعمة البيان وفاضل قبولها بين أهل الإدبار وأهل الإقبال

BIQAI-FULL:v7p402/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402/r7.claim: Al-Raḥīm brings his party near and grants them excellent words and deeds.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402/r7.anchor: { الرحيم } الذي أقبل بأهل حزبه إلى أهل قربه ففازوا بمحاسن الأقوال والأفعال

DURR-FULL:v7p723#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p723#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v7p723#2/r1.claim: When a man said “O Possessor of Majesty and Generosity,” the Prophet told him that his request had been answered and to ask.
DURR-FULL:v7p723#2/r1.anchor: عن معاذ بن جبل قال: سمع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم رجلا يقول: يا ذا الجلال والإكرام قال: قد استجيب لك فسل

DURR-FULL:v7p723#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p723#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v7p723#2/r2.claim: The Prophet says a worshipper's prayer invoking God's praise, oneness, generosity, majesty, and life used God's greatest name, by which He answers and gives.
DURR-FULL:v7p723#2/r2.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك قال: كنت مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم جالسا في الحلقة ورجل قائم يصلي فلما ركع وسجد

DURR-FULL:v7p723#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p723#2/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v7p723#2/r3.claim: After prayer, the Prophet sought forgiveness three times and said that God is peace and the source of peace, blessed as Possessor of Majesty and Generosity.
DURR-FULL:v7p723#2/r3.anchor: عن ثوبان قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا انصرف من صلاته استغفر الله ثلاثا ثم قال: اللهم أنت السلام ومنك السلام

DURR-FULL:v7p723#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p723#2/r4.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v7p723#2/r4.claim: Anas reports the Prophet urged persistent invocation by “O Possessor of Majesty and Generosity,” calling the phrase two of God's greatest names.
DURR-FULL:v7p723#2/r4.anchor: عن أنس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: ألظوا بيا ذا الجلال والإكرام فإنهما اسمان من أسماء الله العظام

DURR-FULL:v7p723#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p723#2/r5.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v7p723#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports the Prophet's instruction to keep invoking “O Possessor of Majesty and Generosity.”
DURR-FULL:v7p723#2/r5.anchor: عن ابن عمر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: ألظوا بيا ذا الجلال والإكرام

DURR-FULL:v7p723#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p723#2/r6.speaker: ربيعة بن عامر
DURR-FULL:v7p723#2/r6.claim: Rabīʿa ibn ʿĀmir says he heard the Prophet urge persistent invocation by “O Possessor of Majesty and Generosity.”
DURR-FULL:v7p723#2/r6.anchor: عن ربيعة بن عامر سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: ألظوا بيا ذا الجلال والإكرام

DURR-FULL:v7p723#2/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p723#2/r7.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v7p723#2/r7.claim: Anas also transmits the Prophet's instruction to keep invoking “O Possessor of Majesty and Generosity.”
DURR-FULL:v7p723#2/r7.anchor: عن أنس أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: ألظوا بيا ذا الجلال والإكرام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p277/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p277/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p277/r1.claim: This metonymy is a subtle rhetorical figure, illustrated by the saying that doubt does not attach to its extremities and by a poem about a house safe from disgrace.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p277/r1.anchor: وهذه الكناية من دقائق الكلام كقولهم : لا يتعلق الشك بأطرافه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p277/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p277/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p277/r2.claim: An anonymous poetic line illustrates the metonymy by describing a household that spends the night safe from blame when other houses incur it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p277/r2.anchor: يبيت بنجاة من اللؤم بيتها إذا ما بيوت بالملامة حلت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p277/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p277/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p277/r3.claim: A parallel distinction appears in ritual purity: most jurists allow reciting Quran without ablution but require ablution to touch the physical muṣḥaf.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p277/r3.anchor: ونظير هذا في التنزيه أن القرآن يقرأ ألفاظه من ليس بمتوضىء ولا يمسك المصحف إلا المتوضىء عند جمهور الفقهاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p277/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p277/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p277/r4.claim: Mentioning the Lord’s name accommodates the preceding divine works and gifts, which words cannot encompass; the hyperbole signals that people owe thanks proportionate to His immense blessings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p277/r4.anchor: فذكر { اسم } في قوله : { تبارك اسم ربك } مراعى فيه أن ما عدد من شؤون الله تعالى ونعمه وإفضاله لا تحيط به العبارة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p277/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p277/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p277/r5.claim: Calling God “your Lord” signals sovereignty joined with compassion and nurture, honors the Prophet through the possessive, and identifies him as the means by which guidance and blessings reached those who feared their Lord.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p277/r5.anchor: وفي استحضار الجلالة بعنوان ( رب ) مضافا إلى ضمير المخاطب وهو النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إشارة إلى ما في معنى الرب من السيادة المشوبة بالرأفة والتنمية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p277/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p277/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p277/r6.claim: Most readers read ذي الجلال in the genitive as an adjective of ربك, while Ibn ʿĀmir reads ذو in the nominative as an adjective of اسم, matching the wording at 55:27; the meaning is the same either way.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p277/r6.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { ذي الجلال } بالياء مجرورا صفة ل { ربك }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p277/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p277/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p277/r7.claim: The consensus to read ذو in the nominative at 55:27, beside the differing transmission of the genitive reading here, suggests وجه denotes the divine essence more directly than اسم.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p277/r7.anchor: ولكن إجماع القراء على رفع { ذو الجلال } الواقع موقع { ويبقى وجه ربك } واختلاف الرواية في جر { ذي الجلال } هنا يشعر بأن لفظ { وجه } أقوى دلالة على الذات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p277/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p277/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p277/r8.claim: A name may mean that blessing comes through uttering God’s names, unlike the enduring “face”; this distinction reflects the wisdom of revelation in seven aḥruf.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p277/r8.anchor: لما علمت من جواز أن يكون المعنى جريان البركة على التلفظ بأسماء الله بخلاف قوله : { ويبقى وجه ربك }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p277/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p277/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p277/r9.claim: Jalāl means greatness encompassing the divine attributes of perfection; ikrām means bestowal of blessing and good, making God worthy of praise and thanks.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p277/r9.anchor: والجلال : العظمة ، وهو جامع لصفات الكمال اللائقة به تعالى . والإكرام : إسداء النعمة والخير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p236#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p236#2/r9.speaker: جمهور الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p236#2/r9.claim: The majority read ذي الجلال in the genitive, agreeing with الرب; Ibn ʿAmir and the Syrians read ذو agreeing with الاسم, also in the first occurrence, while Ubayy and Ibn Masʿud read ذي in both places.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p236#2/r9.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس: «ذي الجلال» على اتباع الرب. وقرأ ابن عامر وأهل الشام. «ذو» على اتباع الاسم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p236#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p236#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p236#2/r10.claim: In this location, الاسم is intended to refer to the named entity itself.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p236#2/r10.anchor: وهذا الموضع مما أريد فيه بالاسم مسماه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p236#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p236#2/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p236#2/r11.claim: Calling upon God with the two names جلال and إكرام is meritorious and likely to be answered; the Prophet urges frequent use of the invocation يا ذا الجلال والإكرام.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p236#2/r11.anchor: والدعاء بهاتين الكلمتين حسن مرجو الإجابة، وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «ألظوا بيا ذا الجلال والإكرام»

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p129/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p129/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p129/r1.claim: One view treats the word name as an added expression, so the meaning is that your Lord is blessed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p129/r1.anchor: أحدهما أن ذكر الاسم صلة والمعنى تبارك ربك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p129/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p129/r2.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p129/r2.claim: Ibn al-Anbari treats name as integral: the form means blessing is obtained and acquired by mentioning God's name.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p129/r2.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري المعنى تفاعل من البركة أي البركة تنال وتكتسب بذكر اسمه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p129/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p129/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p129/r3.claim: The commentary refers to earlier explanations of tabaraka at 7:54 and dhu al-jalal wa-l-ikram at 55:27.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p129/r3.anchor: وقد بينا معنى تبارك في الأعراف 54 وذكرنا في هذه السورة معنى ذي الجلال والإكرام الرحمن 27

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p129/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p129/r4.speaker: ابن عامر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p129/r4.claim: Ibn Amir reads dhu al-jalal in the nominative, matching Syrian codices; the other readers and the Hijazi and Iraqi codices have dhi, while all agree on dhu at the earlier occurrence.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p129/r4.anchor: وكان ابن عامر يقرأ ذو الجلال وكذلك هي في مصاحف أهل الشام والباقون ذي الجلال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p510/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p510/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p510/r1.claim: God deserves reverence without disobedience, worship and gratitude without ingratitude, and remembrance without forgetfulness.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p510/r1.anchor: أي: هو أهل أن يجل فلا يعصى، وأن يكرم فيعبد، ويشكر فلا يكفر، وأن يذكر فلا ينسى.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p510/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p510/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p510/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the Lord of majesty and honor as the possessor of greatness and grandeur.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p510/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: {ذي الجلال والإكرام} ذي العظمة والكبرياء.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p510/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p510/r3.speaker: أبو الدرداء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p510/r3.claim: Abu al-Darda reports a Prophetic supplication: seek or persist in invoking God, and He will forgive you.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p510/r3.anchor: عن أبي العذراء، عن أبي الدرداء، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "أجدوا الله يغفر لكم"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p510/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p510/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p510/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir cites a hadith that honoring an aged Muslim, a person of authority, and a Quran bearer who avoids excess and neglect counts as reverence for God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p510/r4.anchor: وفي الحديث الآخر: "إن من إجلال الله إكرام ذي الشيبة المسلم، وذي السلطان، وحامل القرآن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p510/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p510/r5.speaker: الترمذي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p510/r5.claim: Al-Tirmidhi says Muammil erred in attributing the rare, unpreserved invocation report to Anas; it is instead transmitted from Hamad through Humayd, al-Hasan, and the Prophet.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p510/r5.anchor: ثم قال: غلط المؤمل فيه، وهو غريب وليس بمحفوظ، وإنما يروى هذا عن حماد بن سلمة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p510/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p510/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p510/r6.claim: The Prophet urges repeatedly invoking the Lord of majesty and honor; al-Nasa'i also transmits this report from Rabi'ah through Ibn al-Mubarak.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p510/r6.anchor: عن ربيعة بن عامر قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "ألظوا بذي الجلال والإكرام"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p510/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p510/r7.speaker: الجوهري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p510/r7.claim: Al-Jawhari defines ألظ بفلان as staying close to or adhering to him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p510/r7.anchor: وقال الجوهري: ألظ فلان بفلان: إذا لزمه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p510/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p510/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p510/r8.claim: Ibn Masud glosses the invocation as keeping to it; ilzaz also means persistent insistence.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p510/r8.anchor: وقول ابن مسعود: "ألظوا بيا ذا الجلال والإكرام" أي: الزموا. ويقال: الإلظاظ هو الإلحاح.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p510/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p510/r9.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p510/r9.claim: Ibn Kathir says both glosses are close: continual remembrance, adherence, and insistence.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p510/r9.anchor: قلت: وكلاهما قريب من الآخر -والله أعلم-وهو المداومة واللزوم والإلحاح.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p510/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p510/r10.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p510/r10.claim: Aisha reports that after salutation the Prophet remained seated only long enough to say, God is peace, peace comes from Him, blessed are You, Possessor of majesty and honor.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p510/r10.anchor: من حديث عبد الله بن الحارث، عن عائشة قالت: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا سلم لا يقعد

JISHUMI:v9p6732#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6732#2/r1.speaker: ابن عامر
JISHUMI:v9p6732#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads “dhū al-jalāl” in the nominative as an adjective of “name,” matching the Syrian codices.
JISHUMI:v9p6732#2/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر: ذو الجلال وهي كذلك في مصاحف أهل الشام، على أنه نعت للاسم

JISHUMI:v9p6732#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6732#2/r2.speaker: قراءة الباقين
JISHUMI:v9p6732#2/r2.claim: The other readers use the genitive “dhī al-jalāl,” making it an adjective of the Lord, as in their codices.
JISHUMI:v9p6732#2/r2.anchor: الباقون بالياء على أنه نعت للرب، وكذلك في مصاحفهم

MUQATIL:55:74-78/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:55:74-78/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:55:74-78/r3.claim: The Lord's name is blessed; majesty means greatness and honor means generosity—none is more generous—and God praises Himself.
MUQATIL:55:74-78/r3.anchor: { فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان تبارك اسم ربك ذي الجلال } يعني بالجلال والعظيم { والإكرام } [آية: 78] يعني الكريم

NAHHAS:v4p317/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p317/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p317/r10.claim: Blessing in God's name means the persistence and stability of favor; the verse urges abundant invocation and supplication by His name with reverence and exaltation.
NAHHAS:v4p317/r10.anchor: البركة في اللغة بقاء النعمة وثباتها فحضهم بهذا على أن يكثروا ذكر اسمه

NAHHAS:v4p317/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p317/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p317/r11.claim: ذي الجلال والإكرام means the Majestic and Generous.
NAHHAS:v4p317/r11.anchor: فقال ( ذي الجلال والإكرام ) أي الجليل الكريم

NAHHAS:v4p317/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p317/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p317/r12.claim: A hadith recommends persistently invoking God as ذا الجلال والإكرام.
NAHHAS:v4p317/r12.anchor: وفي الحديث ألظوا بياذا الجلال والإكرام

NASAFI-FULL:v4p205#21/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p205#21/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p205#21/r1.claim: The descriptive phrase dhul-jalal is read in the Syrian tradition as an adjective of the name.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p205#21/r1.anchor: لعظمة ذو الجال شامى صفة للاسم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p205#21/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p205#21/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p205#21/r2.claim: God's majesty and generosity are bestowed on His faithful servants through His beneficence.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p205#21/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p205#21/r3.speaker: جابر
NASAFI-FULL:v4p205#21/r3.claim: Jabir reports that the Prophet recited Surat al-Rahman and chided silent listeners, saying the jinn had responded better.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p205#21/r3.anchor: روى جابر ان النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p205#21/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p205#21/r4.speaker: جابر
NASAFI-FULL:v4p205#21/r4.claim: Jabir's report says that whenever the Prophet recited the refrain, the jinn answered that they denied none of God's favors and praised and thanked Him.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p205#21/r4.anchor: ما ايمت على قول الله فبأى آلاء ربكما تكذبان الا قالوا ولا بشىء من نعمك ربنا نكذب فلك الحمد ولك الشكر

NASAFI-FULL:v4p205#21/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p205#21/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p205#21/r5.claim: The refrain occurs thirty-one times: eight follow signs of creation and the beginning and end of creation, seven follow descriptions of Hell and its terrors, then eight describe each of two pairs of gardens.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p205#21/r5.anchor: وكررت هذه الاية في هذه السورة احدى وثلاثين مرة ذكر ثمانية منها عقب آيات فيها تعداد عجائب خلق الله وبدائع صنعه ومبدا الخلق ومعادهم ثم سبعة منها عقب آيات فيها ذكر انار وشدائدها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p205#21/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p205#21/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p205#21/r6.claim: The eight initial refrains are tied to the gates of Paradise and Hell: one who believes them and acts accordingly has Paradise's gates opened and Hell's closed.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p205#21/r6.anchor: فمن اعتقد الثمانية الاولى وعمل بموجبها فتحت له ابواب الجنة واغلقت عنه ابواب جهنم

QURTUBI-FULL:55:76-78#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:76-78#2/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:55:76-78#2/r10.claim: Tabāraka is the tafaʿāla form of baraka; al-jalāl means majesty, as discussed earlier.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:76-78#2/r10.anchor: تبارك } تفاعل من البركة وقد تقدم. { ذي الجلال } أي العظمة. وقد تقدم

QURTUBI-FULL:55:76-78#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:76-78#2/r11.speaker: عامر
QURTUBI-FULL:55:76-78#2/r11.claim: ʿĀmir reads ذو الجلال with nominative wāw and makes it an adjective of “the Name,” supporting the view that the Name is the named reality.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:76-78#2/r11.anchor: وقرأ عامر «ذو الجلال» بالواو وجعله وصفا للاسم، وذلك تقوية لكون الاسم هو المسمى

QURTUBI-FULL:55:76-78#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:76-78#2/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:55:76-78#2/r12.claim: The other readers use genitive ذي as an adjective of “your Lord”; the phrase points back to al-Raḥmān, the name opening the sura.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:76-78#2/r12.anchor: الباقون { ذي الجلال } جعلوا «ذي» صفة ل { ربك }. وكأنه يريد به الاسم الذي افتتح به السورة

QURTUBI-FULL:55:76-78#2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:76-78#2/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:55:76-78#2/r13.claim: The sura recounts creation by mercy, divine governance, the Resurrection, Hell, and Paradise, then praises the name al-Raḥmān as the source of creation and mercy; God is majestic in Himself and generous in His acts.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:76-78#2/r13.anchor: هذا كله خرج لكم من رحمتي، فمن رحمتي خلقتكم وخلقت لكم السماء والأرض والخلق والخليقة

QURTUBI-FULL:55:76-78#2/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:76-78#2/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:55:76-78#2/r14.claim: All readers agree on the nominative adjective-form at the opening; Qurṭubī takes it to signal the divine Face that believers will see and joyfully meet.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:76-78#2/r14.anchor: ولم يختلف القراء في إجراء النعت على الوجه بالرفع في أول السورة، وهو يدل على أن المراد به وجه الله

RAZI-FULL:v29p120/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p120/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p120/r1.claim: The closing pairing sets the world’s favors against the afterlife’s: only God is self-subsistent, while the world perishes and the hereafter lasts only because God preserves it.
RAZI-FULL:v29p120/r1.anchor: إشارة إلى أن الباقي والدائم لذاته هو الله تعالى لا غير والدنيا فانية ، والآخرة وإن كانت باقية لكن بقاؤها بإبقاء الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v29p120/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p120/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p120/r2.claim: The surahs end by naming God: after al-Qamar’s ‘Sovereign, Powerful,’ this surah says remembrance of God is the highest favor and most complete pleasure.
RAZI-FULL:v29p120/r2.anchor: بعد ذكر الجنات وما فيها من النعم قال : { تبارك اسم ربك ذى الجلال والإكرام } إشارة إلى أن أتم النعم عند الله تعالى ، وأكمل اللذات ذكر الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v29p120/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p120/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p120/r3.claim: The next surah similarly closes with glorification of God after mentioning spirit, fragrance, and a garden of delight.
RAZI-FULL:v29p120/r3.anchor: فروح وريحان * وجنة * نعيم } ( الواقعة : 89 ) ثم قال تعالى في آخر السورة : { فسبح باسم ربك العظيم }

RAZI-FULL:v29p120/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p120/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p120/r4.claim: The gardens’ description omits hearing, one of the greatest pleasures; reclining on green couches, their people hear God’s remembrance.
RAZI-FULL:v29p120/r4.anchor: لم يذكر لذة السماع وهي من أتم أنواعها ، فقال : { متكئين على رفرف خضر } يسمعون ذكر الله

RAZI-FULL:v29p120/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p120/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p120/r5.claim: Tabāraka derives from baraka, permanence and stability, as in a camel kneeling and water collecting in a pool.
RAZI-FULL:v29p120/r5.anchor: أصل التبارك من البركة وهي الدوام والثبات ، ومنها بروك البعير وبركة الماء

RAZI-FULL:v29p120/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p120/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p120/r6.claim: One meaning is that God’s name endures and remains established.

RAZI-FULL:v29p120/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p120/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p120/r7.claim: A second meaning is that goodness continually abides with God, since baraka is also used for good.
RAZI-FULL:v29p120/r7.anchor: دام الخير عنده لأن البركة وإن كانت من الثبات لكنها تستعمل في الخير

RAZI-FULL:v29p120/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p120/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p120/r8.claim: A third meaning is exaltation in rank, not elevation in place.
RAZI-FULL:v29p120/r8.anchor: تبارك بمعنى علا وارتفع شأنا لا مكانا

RAZI-FULL:v29p120/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p120/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p120/r9.claim: After worldly favors the text says God’s face remains because all possible beings perish in themselves; afterlife residents endure by God’s sustaining power and take pleasure in remembering His name.
RAZI-FULL:v29p120/r9.anchor: وقعت إلى أن بقاء أهل الجنة بإبقاء الله ذاكرين اسم الله متلذذين به فقال : { تبارك اسم ربك }

RAZI-FULL:v29p120/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p120/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p120/r10.claim: In that afterlife no name but God’s remains on people’s tongues; they have no need of one another and fear no one, and their conversations invoke God.
RAZI-FULL:v29p120/r10.anchor: في ذلك اليوم لا يبقى اسم أحد إلا اسم الله تعالى به تدور الألسن ولا يكون لأحد عند أحد حاجة

RAZI-FULL:v29p120#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p120#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p120#2/r1.claim: The common view treats ‘name’ as redundant, like ‘face’ in the prior verse, supported by other Qur’anic uses of tabāraka without ‘name.’
RAZI-FULL:v29p120#2/r1.anchor: وهو المشهور أنه مقحم كالوجه في قوله تعالى : { ويبقى وجه ربك } يدل عليه قوله : { فتبارك الله أحسن الخالقين }

RAZI-FULL:v29p120#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p120#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p120#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, the name itself is blessed: if tabāraka means exalted, elevation of the name points to still greater elevation of its bearer, as royal protocol shows.
RAZI-FULL:v29p120#2/r2.anchor: هو أن الاسم تبارك ، وفيه إشارة إلى معنى بليغ ، أما إذا قلنا : تبارك بمعنى علا فمن علا اسمه كيف يكون مسماه

RAZI-FULL:v29p120#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p120#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p120#2/r3.claim: If tabāraka means that goodness remains with God, invoking His name removes evil, drives Satan away, increases good, and draws happiness near.
RAZI-FULL:v29p120#2/r3.anchor: فهو إشارة إلى أن ذكر اسم الله تعالى يزيل الشر ويهرب الشيطان ويزيد الخير ويقرب السعادات

RAZI-FULL:v29p120#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p120#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p120#2/r4.claim: If it means that God’s name endures, it points to the continued remembrance of God by paradise’s inhabitants.
RAZI-FULL:v29p120#2/r4.anchor: فهو إشارة إلى دوام الذاكرين في الجنة على ما قلنا من قبل

RAZI-FULL:v29p120#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p120#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p120#2/r5.claim: The common reading here is ذي الجلال, while 55:27 reads ذو الجلال: glory belongs to the Lord, and the name is distinct from its bearer, whereas the Lord’s face is the Lord.
RAZI-FULL:v29p120#2/r5.anchor: القراءة المشهورة ههنا : { ذى الجلال } وفي قوله تعالى : { ويبقى وجه ربك ذو الجلال }

RAZI-FULL:v29p120#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p120#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p120#2/r6.claim: Calling the surviving entity ‘the Lord’ might imply He remains as Lord with a subject; saying ‘His face’ removes that implication and asserts the Real’s absolute permanence.
RAZI-FULL:v29p120#2/r6.anchor: لو قال : ويبقى الرب لتوهم أن الرب إذا بقي ربا فله في ذلك الزمان مربوب

STUDYQURAN:55:78/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:78/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:55:78/r1.claim: The phrase “Possessed of Majesty and Bounty” closes the discussion of heavenly blessings, echoing its role at 55:27 for earthly blessings.
STUDYQURAN:55:78/r1.anchor: here it marks the end of the discussion of heavenly blessings.

STUDYQURAN:55:78/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:78/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:55:78/r2.claim: Here the phrase modifies “thy Lord,” as it modified “the Face of thy Lord” at 55:27.
STUDYQURAN:55:78/r2.anchor: Here it modifies thy Lord, just as it modified the Face of thy Lord in v. 27.

STUDYQURAN:55:78/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:78/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:55:78/r3.claim: A canonical reading construes “Possessed of Majesty and Bounty” as modifying “Name,” reading dhū rather than dhī.
STUDYQURAN:55:78/r3.anchor: According to another canonical reading, Possessed of Majesty and Bounty could here be read as modifying the Name (i.e., dhū, rather than dhī; Q, Z).

STUDYQURAN:55:78/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:78/r4.speaker: Prophet
STUDYQURAN:55:78/r4.claim: The Prophet advised followers to persist in invoking “O Possessor of Majesty and Bounty.”
STUDYQURAN:55:78/r4.anchor: It is said that the Prophet advised his followers, “Persist [in invoking] ‘O Possessor of Majesty and Bounty’” (IK).

STUDYQURAN:55:78/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:78/r5.speaker: ʿĀʾishah
STUDYQURAN:55:78/r5.claim: An account attributed to ʿĀʾishah says the Prophet often prayed after prayers, “O God, Thou art Peace, and peace comes from Thee. Blessed art Thou, Possessed of Majesty and Bounty.”
STUDYQURAN:55:78/r5.anchor: account attributed toʿĀʾishah that after prayers the Prophet would often sit and say

TAB-FULL:v22p278#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p278#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p278#2/r1.claim: The author glosses Dhu al-jalal as majesty; Ibn Abbas’s report expands this as majesty and greatness.
TAB-FULL:v22p278#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {ذي الجلال والإكرام} [الرحمن: 78] يقول: «ذو العظمة والكبرياء»

TAB-FULL:v22p278#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p278#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v22p278#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses Dhu al-Jalal wa-al-Ikram as the possessor of majesty and greatness.
TAB-FULL:v22p278#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {ذي الجلال والإكرام} [الرحمن: 78] يقول: «ذو العظمة والكبرياء»

SAMIN-DURR:55:78/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:78/r1.speaker: ابن عامر
SAMIN-DURR:55:78/r1.claim: Ibn Amir reads ذو in the nominative as an adjective following the divine name, matching the Syrian codex; the other readers use genitive ذي as an adjective of the Lord, who is described.
SAMIN-DURR:55:78/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر " ذو الجلال " بالواو، وجعله تابعا للاسم، وهكذا هي مرسومة في مصحف الشاميين.

TABATABAI:55:78/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:78/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:78/r2.claim: The closing praise celebrates God because both worlds overflow with blessings from His vast mercy; the blessed name is al-Rahman, the sura’s opening name, and baraka is abundant good issuing from Him.
TABATABAI:55:78/r2.anchor: وبذلك يظهر أن المراد باسمه المتبارك هو الرحمن المفتتحة به السورة، والتبارك كثرة الخيرات والبركات الصادرة

TABATABAI:55:78/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:78/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:78/r3.claim: “Possessor of majesty and honor” points to God’s beautiful names and attributes; these qualities shape His acts, from creation and wise ordering to rewarding obedience and punishing wrongdoing, so His blessings bear their imprint.
TABATABAI:55:78/r3.anchor: ولصفات الفاعل ظهور في أفعاله وأثر فيها يرتبط به الفعل بفاعله فهو تعالى خلق الخلق ونظم النظام

TABRISI:55:62-78/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:62-78/r1.speaker: ابن عامر
TABRISI:55:62-78/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAmir reads dhū al-jalāl in the nominative; the other readers read dhī in the genitive.
TABRISI:55:62-78/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر ذو الجلال بالرفع والباقون بالجر

TABRISI:55:62-78/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:62-78/r4.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:55:62-78/r4.claim: With the genitive reading, dhī is an adjective modifying rabbak.
TABRISI:55:62-78/r4.anchor: من قرأ ذي الجلال فجر جعله صفة لربك

TABRISI:55:62-78/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:62-78/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
TABRISI:55:62-78/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿud is reported to read “your Lord’s face, possessor of majesty and honor,” with both instances in the genitive.
TABRISI:55:62-78/r5.anchor: وزعموا أن ابن مسعود قرأ ويبقى وجه ربك ذي الجلال والإكرام بالياء في كلتيهما

TABRISI:55:62-78/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:62-78/r6.speaker: الأصمعي
TABRISI:55:62-78/r6.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿi says jalāl is used only of God, supporting the genitive reading, though the source counters with poetry using it of others.
TABRISI:55:62-78/r6.anchor: لا يقال الجلال إلا في الله تعالى فهذا يقوي الجر

TABRISI:55:62-78/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:62-78/r7.speaker: ابن جني
TABRISI:55:62-78/r7.claim: For the nominative reading, Ibn Jinni says the word is coordinated with the noun.
TABRISI:55:62-78/r7.anchor: ومن رفع أجراه على الاسم قال ابن جني

TABRISI:55:72-78/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:72-78/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:55:72-78/r14.claim: Tabāraka means that the Lord’s name is exalted and high, since God alone deserves attributes such as being eternal, deity, self-powerful, self-knowing, and living.
TABRISI:55:72-78/r14.anchor: { تبارك اسم ربك } أي تعاظم وتعالى اسم ربك لأنه استحق أن يوصف

TABRISI:55:72-78/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:72-78/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:55:72-78/r15.claim: Dhū al-jalāl means possessing greatness and majesty.
TABRISI:55:72-78/r15.anchor: { ذي الجلال } أي ذي العظمة والكبرياء

TABRISI:55:72-78/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:72-78/r16.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:55:72-78/r16.claim: Al-Hasan explains al-ikrām as God honoring the people of His religion and allegiance.
TABRISI:55:72-78/r16.anchor: { والإكرام } يكرم أهل دينه وولايته عن الحسن.

TABRISI:55:72-78/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:72-78/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:55:72-78/r17.claim: Another interpretation finds abundant blessing in the Lord’s name and urges seeking blessing in everything by mentioning it.
TABRISI:55:72-78/r17.anchor: معناه عظمة البركة في اسم ربك فاطلبوا البركة في كل شيء بذكر اسمه.

TABRISI:55:72-78/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:72-78/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:55:72-78/r18.claim: Another interpretation treats “name” as an added expression for the meaning “may your Lord be blessed,” illustrated with a line by Labid.
TABRISI:55:72-78/r18.anchor: إن اسم صلة لمعنى تبارك ربك قال لبيد:

TABRISI:55:72-78/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:72-78/r19.speaker: author
TABRISI:55:72-78/r19.claim: Another interpretation says God’s name is free of every evil and that He has the most beautiful names.
TABRISI:55:72-78/r19.anchor: إن المعنى أن اسمه منزه عن كل سوء له الأسماء الحسنى

TABRISI:55:62-78#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:62-78#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:55:62-78#2/r1.claim: The Prophet taught people to keep invoking God as “Possessor of Majesty and Honor.”

ZAJJAJ:v5p105/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p105/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p105/r4.claim: The surah closes by declaring what is fitting for God: that He be glorified and magnified.
ZAJJAJ:v5p105/r4.anchor: فإنما ينبغي أن يعظما الله ويمجداه، فختم السورة بما ينبغي أن يمجد به

THALABI:v9p198/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p198/r5.speaker: أبو بكرة
THALABI:v9p198/r5.claim: Abu Bakra reports that the Prophet's recitation joined the phrases with waw, including rafraf khudr wa-abqariyy hissan and the final doxology; this is the Syrian reading in their codices.
THALABI:v9p198/r5.anchor: عن عاصم الجحدري عن أبي بكرة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأ (متكئين على رفرف خضر وعباقري حسان

THALABI:v9p198/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p198/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p198/r6.claim: The Syrian reading has ذو in the nominative in the final phrase, while the other readers have ذي in the genitive.
THALABI:v9p198/r6.anchor: تبارك اسم ربك ذو الجلال والإكرام) بالواو، شامي وكذلك هو في مصاحفهم. الباقون: (ذي الجلال والإكرام)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p206/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p206/r1.speaker: ابن عامر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p206/r1.claim: He reads “dhu al-jalal” in the nominative, making it agree with “name”; this indicates that the name is the named one, since majesty is God’s attribute, not an attribute of naming.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:76-78/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:76-78/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:76-78/r4.claim: The surah closes with words fitting to glorify and exalt God.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:76-78/r4.anchor: ثم ختم السورة بما ينبغي أن يمجد به ويعظم

NASHR:v2p382/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p382/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p382/r1.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads the final occurrence as dhu al-jalāl, with wāw, making it an adjective of the Lord; his codices also have that form.
NASHR:v2p382/r1.anchor: بواو بعد الذال نعتا للرب، وكذلك هو في مصاحفهم.

DAMGHANI:v1p246/r4.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p246/r4.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p246/r4.claim: Ism can mean the named one itself: “the name of your Lord” means your Lord.
DAMGHANI:v1p246/r4.anchor: فوجه منها : الاسم يعني المسمى فذلك قوله تعالى في سورة الرحمن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r5.claim: The sura ends by glorifying and praising God.
